rationale: The defining study establishing Intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 73 (OMIM #620450 / TAF4-related NDD; Janssen et al., 2022) exclusively identifies de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF / truncating) variants in an initial cohort of eight individuals. There is no empirical literature in the provided evidence base documenting pathogenic missense variants clustering within the TAF4 histone-fold or TAF-homology domains that cause transcriptional pause/escape disruption resulting in phenotypes indistinguishable from truncating alleles.

evidence.text: Janssen et al. (2022) report eight individuals with de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 presenting with a neurodevelopmental disorder (T4NDD) characterized by intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphism, establishing haploinsufficiency/loss-of-function rather than domain-clustered missense variants as the etiology.

source.title: De novo putative loss-of-function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro-developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms. We propose TAF4 as a novel dominant disease gene for NDD, and coin this novel disorder 'TAF4-related NDD' (T4NDD).

evidence.text: Genomics England PanelApp curates TAF4 for intellectual disability under OMIM #620450 based on mouse knockout models and human loss-of-function evidence without establishing pathogenic missense variation in specific structural domains.

source.title: Gene: TAF4 (Intellectual disability)
source.quote: The mouse knockout shows there is an effect of loss of TAF4 but the phenotype ... Intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 73, OMIM:620450.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits that missense variants clustering in the histone-fold and TAF-homology domains cause disease via transcriptional pause/escape disruption indistinguishable from truncating alleles; however, established cohort reports identify exclusively de novo putative loss-of-function (truncating/splice) mutations in TAF4.

new_directions.question_text: Do rare de novo missense variants in the histone-fold domain or TAF-homology domain of TAF4 destabilize TFIID assembly or alter core promoter recognition in patient cohorts with unexplained neurodevelopmental disorders?
new_directions.rationale: While current diagnostic criteria rely on putative loss-of-function variants, structural missense alterations might act via dominant-negative or hypomorphic mechanisms that remain uncharacterized.

new_directions.question_text: What is the precise phenotypic breakdown (HPO terms with exact numerators and denominators) across multicenter expanded cohorts of TAF4-related NDD?
new_directions.rationale: Differentiating TAF4-related NDD from other TFIID subunit-associated disorders (TAF-opathies) requires granular clinical delineation beyond initial small-cohort case series.
